youtube.title: Why the Hook on Your Tape Measure Is Loose 📏 #Shorts #science #facts #didyouknow
youtube.description:
The metal hook at the end of a tape measure is loose on purpose. It slides back and forth by exactly the thickness of the hook. When you hook it over an edge and pull, it slides out so the measurement starts right at the edge. When you push it against a wall, it slides in so the measurement starts at the hook's outer face. Either way you get a true reading, so never tighten those rivets.

Subscribe to The Hidden Why for a new why every day.

sources: Tape measure makers (e.g. Stanley): the 'true zero' sliding hook moves by its own thickness for inside and outside measurements
